title: Products of affine scheme morphisms exist
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $J$ be a small set, and let $g_j:T_j\to S$ be affine morphisms for $j\in J$. The product $T=\prod_{j\in J}T_j$ exists in the category of schemes over $S$; it is the inverse limit of the finite fibre products, and its projections to every finite fibre product are affine.

proof.text: For each finite subset $F\subseteq J$, construct an $S$-scheme $P_F$ with the universal property of the finite product of $(T_j)_{j\in F}$ in schemes over $S$. Induct on $|F|$: for $F=\varnothing$ use $P_\varnothing=S$ and its identity structure map, which is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. If $j\notin E$, form $P_{E\cup\{j\}}=P_E\times_ST_j$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Maps over $S$ into this pullback are exactly a map into $P_E$ and a map into $T_j$, so its universal property is the required one. Its projection to $P_E$ is affine by the base-change clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], applied to $g_j:T_j\to S$. Its structure map to $S$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-composition] and the induction hypothesis. Thus every $P_F\to S$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0CNI, lemma-infinite-product, proof hint using Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit)

proof.text: For $F\subseteq G$, define $r_{GF}:P_G\to P_F$ over $S$ by forgetting the coordinates outside $F$. The finite-product universal properties give $r_{FF}=1$ and $r_{HF}=r_{GF}r_{HG}$ for $F\subseteq G\subseteq H$, since their composites to every factor agree. They also identify $P_G$ with $P_F\times_SP_{G\setminus F}$, with $r_{GF}$ the first projection: maps to either side are exactly maps to all factors indexed by $G$. This is a base-change square for the affine map $P_{G\setminus F}\to S$ of Step 1. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] therefore makes $r_{GF}$ affine. The finite subsets of the small set $J$ form a small nonempty directed poset (the empty subset is an element and $F\cup G$ is an upper bound). Thus $(P_F,r_{GF})$ is a small directed inverse system with affine transition morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CNI, lemma-infinite-product, proof hint using Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] to this directed inverse system. There exists a scheme limit $T=\varprojlim_F P_F$ with compatible legs $p_F:T\to P_F$, and every $p_F$ is affine. Let $t=p_\varnothing:T\to S$ be its structure morphism. Compatibility for $\varnothing\subseteq F$ makes every $p_F$ an $S$-morphism. The singleton legs are consequently $S$-morphisms $\pi_j:T\to T_j$, using the canonical identification $P_{\{j\}}=T_j$.

source.place: Tag 0CNI, lemma-infinite-product, proof hint using Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit)

proof.text: Fix any $S$-scheme $a:Y\to S$. For a family of $S$-morphisms $h_j:Y\to T_j$, the finite-product universal properties from Step 1 give unique $S$-morphisms $h_F:Y\to P_F$ with these coordinates; for the empty subset take $h_\varnothing=a$. Forgetting coordinates shows $r_{GF}h_G=h_F$. The limit universal property gives a unique scheme morphism $h:Y\to T$ with $p_Fh=h_F$ for every $F$. At $F=\varnothing$ this gives $th=a$, so $h$ is over $S$, and at singletons it gives $\pi_jh=h_j$. Conversely, any $S$-morphism with these singleton composites has the same composites to every $P_F$ by finite-product uniqueness, hence equals $h$ by limit uniqueness. Thus $T$ is the product in schemes over $S$, and the limit construction already gives its stated finite-product description and affine projections. If $J$ is empty this proof gives $T=S$ with its terminal property over $S$.
